title: Hackers reportedly set cold rooms to 100 degrees at Slovenian meat processor Alpija
date_note: Pages give only their publication day (27 Nov); the day of the attack is not stated.
geo_basis: Town named by the sources (Tolmin / Tolmino)
summary: Open reports that Alpija director Nikola Šavle told the Slovenian site 24ur.com that hackers raised the temperature of refrigerators and cold rooms holding cured meats worth "250mila euro". An employee noticed a cold room set to "100 gradi", and a technician found an IT lock with a photo of Matteo Salvini on screen. Open says police in Nova Gorica are investigating and nobody has claimed the attack.
plain: Open reports hackers changed the settings of cold rooms at a Slovenian meat plant, Alpija, and left a photo of Matteo Salvini on screen. Police are investigating and no one has claimed it, Open says.
exec: Open reports an intrusion into refrigeration controls at a food producer put cured meats worth "250mila euro" at risk; police are investigating.

evidence.quote: impostando la temperatura di diversi frigoriferi e celle frigorifere a 100 gradi Celsius

validation.note: Open (citing 24ur.com) and StrettoWeb (no source named) both relay the same account; the 24ur original, corriere.it (not loadable) and any Alpija or police statement were not read.
